utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, yes. You are to continue with your examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we went through those videotapes and reviewed your report that you sent from the on-site investigation in Racak village. William Walker was in Racak on the 16th when fire was opened on you and you were unable to reach the village. You drafted the report that we quoted here after the 15th, on the 17th and 18th. Tell me, was Walker able to see everything that you saw; the trenches, the ammunition that was used, military equipment, the KLA base, everything that you found there on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: My understanding was that you didn't actually see Mr. Walker there, that you learned about his presence from a newspaper report or a television report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I saw him on TV, actually. May I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since Walker was in Racak, I suppose that he was able to see all the things that I saw, at least the trenches, because the trenches criss-crossed the hill from every direction. I don't know from which side exactly he entered Racak, but since trenches are in many places, I suppose he saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "trenches," you mean also the military equipment, the materiel that could be seen, the casings for Chinese-made weapons, doubtlessly from the arsenal of the Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you're offending the rule against leading questions. Either you can conduct the examination in chief or you can't conduct it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just derive one fact that is certain: Walker seems to have seen things that you didn't see, and you saw things that he didn't see. That's what seems to come up, and you were in the same place.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see the things that Walker says to have seen, on television, since I tried to enter Racak with my team and fire was opened on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that already. Walker was in Racak. That's one thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm now lost. What is it you say Mr. Walker claims to have seen that you did not see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see what I saw on television and the version that Walker presented on TV, namely the ditch with the corpses and the unbelievable news that the police had committed the massacre of civilians in Racak. I didn't see that when I came for the on-site investigation. I tried to reach the spot where those corpses allegedly lay. We toured the entire village of Racak. We didn't see that spot. We didn't see any traces of blood, nothing of what Walker spoke about on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mrs. Marinkovic. Since we were able to see the police entering Racak on the videotape, we could see the vehicles of the Verification Mission on the hill overlooking the village, we could see the things that the Reuters cameraman filmed that morning, and we could see that there was ammunition, weapons, and all the things that you found on your tour of the village, was there any grounds for the claim that the police had massacred civilians in Racak?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. She can't answer that, Mr. Milosevic. If you are unable to conduct the examination-in-chief, I'll ask the assigned counsel to take over.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, you ordered that the victims from the mosque should be transported away, that the forensic expertise should be performed. Were all these killed in Racak identified?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should like the Trial Chamber to permit me to answer the previous question and to present certain observations that I wanted to present yesterday during the viewing of the videotapes. The session ended precisely at that moment, and I wanted to say because I was on the spot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. I've already ruled that that question is not to be answered, and it's not a ruling that I will reconsider.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we entered Racak and when we entered the mosque, we found 40 bodies. We entered the mosque together with the representatives of the OSCE who were with me, and with other on-site investigation team members and representatives of the press whom I allowed in to film briefly and then leave so that we could conduct our official business. All the bodies found in the mosque, all the 40 bodies were marked, according to procedure, with numbers. Our forensic expert, Mr. Dobricanin, Professor Dobricanin, viewed the bodies and tried to see if there are any traces of massacre, if there are any visible signs of massacre, and then the bodies were transported in a vehicle that was intended --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question was whether the bodies were identified.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to give you the whole story as things were done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your task here is to answer the questions that are actually asked. I know it's a system you're not familiar with, but the system here is that the witness -- the examiner asks the questions and the witness answers what's asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Marinkovic, since pursuant to that procedure which you described, you transported the victims to the Institute for Forensic Medicine, tell me, were all those bodies identified?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they identified according to the rules of forensic medicine, including the taking of prints, inspection of all ID papers found on them?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were identified pursuant to the law and our procedure, all the rules of investigation, and all the bodies were identified, all 40 of them. I issued an order to the SUP of Pristina to comply with my order, and part of that order was to identify all the bodies we found in the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, when was it that you saw those bodies at the mosque? Could you give me the date and time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We saw the bodies on the 18th of January, 1999, when we arrived at Racak village. It could have been 11.00, 11.30, maybe noon. The time is marked in my on-site investigation report. I cannot tell you the exact time now when we entered the mosque. There is a record of the investigation on-site dated the 14th of January. Sorry, dated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Up until that time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- dated the 18th of January, and the number -- the number is 14/99.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So up until that time you were not able to enter the village, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was not allowed to go into the village. It was impossible for me to go into the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just let's have one thing clear with regard to Mr. Kwon's question. You entered the village on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the first time. I explained that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you included that in your report when you found the weapons, the ammunition, et cetera, then fire was opened upon you. The 16th you were not able to go in. On the 18th you wrote in your report what you were able to do. That was the first occasion when you could see the bodies, the 18th.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On my -- in my Official Note dated the 15th of January, all of that is written. I performed only one part of my on-site investigation on the 15th. I found the weapons on the 15th and then fire was opened upon us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On the 15th, when the incident happened, you started your investigation, and you finished it on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In view of the circumstances you already described.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you in this connection how the bodies were identified, and you told me all of them were identified. Now, since you have a list of all of the identified bodies, all 40 of them, my question is: Do those names coincide with the names contained in the annex to the indictment related to Racak?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just take a copy of the indictment to compare the list? This is my list that I have, and it is already provided to the Office of the Prosecutor. I can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters would kindly ask the accused and the witness to slow down a little. This is very important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic and Mrs. Marinkovic, the interpreters are asking you once again to speak more slowly. That will facilitate the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, please give us the briefest possible answer. The list that you have here on page 41, where it says Annex A, persons killed in Racak, the 15th of January, 1999, so this is a list, and does this list coincide with your list of 40 persons who ended up at the Forensic Medicine Institute on your orders?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the list that I have in terms of the identification of the bodies that were found in the mosque in Racak, and it is 40 bodies, when I compared the names to the list on page 41 of the indictment, 36 bodies match the names mentioned in my list, and the names mentioned in the indictment, that is. However, in the indictment, there are no details, only names and surnames, and in some cases the age is mentioned as well. However, in my list, there is also the date of birth, the place of birth, the father's name, and where the said person came from. Now, what does not match in terms of my list and the list in the indictment is nine persons who are in Schedule A of the indictment. I do not have them on my list, so this is nine persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So nine are not in the 40 that you found.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they are in Schedule A in that list?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And four persons mentioned on my list who are identified with the other persons are not in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you tell me when that list was supplied to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume with the other evidence that has to do with Racak, when it was handed over to the Office of the Prosecutor, when the Office of the Prosecutor asked for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. All 40 that were found were identified. They were fingerprinted, full identification was carried out, all their details were provided, and practically four plus nine is 13 and that is the difference between the two lists?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There are nine persons here who are not among the 40 who had been killed in Racak, and there are four who are not on this list but who are on your list?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And I wish to add something else in terms of identification, that the next of kin of the killed persons came to the Forensic Medicine Institute directly to take the bodies of their nearest and dearest. And before a kinsman would identify a body, I would compile a record, and this record would be made when the bodies were identified, and on the 10th of February, 1999, the family members of the victims were there and they signed the record stating that they took the bodies of their family members, and this is part of the documentation that has to do with what happened in the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd like you to tell me slowly the names of the nine persons who are not on the Prosecution's Schedule A but are on your list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The nine persons who are on the Prosecution's list but not on your list. Just tell me the names slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Aslani Ljuta [phoen], it says here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Aslani Ljuta, for the first one. And the second one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Emini Ajet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the interpreter help me with that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: E-m-i-n-i.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Third?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ibrahimi Hajris [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Four.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ismaili Mejha [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ismaili Muhamet [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Six.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mustafa Ahmet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next one, seven.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Salihu Jashar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Eight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Salihu Shurri. And another name up here, Azemi Banush [phoen]. It's the second person on the list, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. And then the four -- and then you said there were four on your list but not on the Prosecution Schedule A. Give me the names of those four.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Kamberi Banush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Kamberi Banush.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a K. Kamberi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Smajli Mehmet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note the first letter is S, it starts with an S. It's just Smajli, not Ismajli.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Third.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Brahimi Ajet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Brahimi... I'm looking for the spelling on the transcript, Ajet? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In some cases it's Hajet, in other cases it's Ajet, but sometimes it's with an H and sometimes without an H, but most probably it is A-j-e-t.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sula Sabri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When did you first discover this discrepancy between your list and the list on the -- in Schedule A of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, when we were in contact and when we were preparing the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, you know that Western sources, starting from Walker, made it public that women, children, old men were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, put your questions properly. Put your questions properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, on your list are there any women; and if so, how many are there? When I say "your list," I'm referring to the list compiled by the forensic experts from our country, from Belorussia, and from Finland. Are there any women?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us her name?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 36, Mehmeti Hanamushahir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So it's one woman.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you establish through your own investigation whether that woman was a member of the KLA or not?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the pre-trial proceedings, on the basis of the information I received, and also after what happened in Racak, I received information and I came to know that she was one of the members of the KLA in the village of Racak, together with her three brothers and their father who was commander of the KLA staff in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Children and old men were mentioned in the public. A German journalist, Bo Adam, testified here. He investigated Racak. He testified about this, and he said that one young boy who got killed was killed by gunfire coming from the hill on the other side of the valley. Are there any other children who were victims?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Apart from that boy, there are none. We identified the boy as being between age 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So all the others were men.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In your investigation, did you establish that these were members of the KLA, or were they civilians?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the investigation process that I carried out on site when I carried out the on-site investigation on that day when the place was made accessible to me, and before that on the 15th when I found a large quantity of weapons, after that day we toured the entire area. We found the trenches, their headquarters. And all the material evidence that I found in the field directly as an investigating judge I entered in the official record in the presence of all other members of the investigation team, in the presence of the OSCE monitors, who were with me all the time as we could see yesterday on the video footage, and I explained as we were going along all of this to them too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The question was whether you're able to establish that they were members of the KLA or whether they were civilians. Were you able to establish that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. I managed to establish that they were members of a terrorist gang that was operating in Racak. They were not civilians. That is why I mentioned all the things I did in terms of material evidence, and also later on, before the police started their planned action, there was knowledge that Racak was a major stronghold of terrorists in the area. I received information immediately on the 15th about that from the policeman. And if you wish, I can show you my handwritten note that I wrote on that day, that very day, the 15th, when I first got there. This is from my own notebook, everything that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just give us concisely the bases for your conclusion that they were members of the KLA, the terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the basis of the information collected in the pre-trial proceedings by the authorised personnel of SUP Urosevac and before the action took place in Racak and after that. In that period, in October and September 1998, the terrorists kidnapped and abducted both Serbs and Albanians. They were killing policemen, and immediate grounds why the police took action was the fact that in the village of Slilovo [phoen] on the 10th of January the police vehicle was shot at, a police vehicle from the police station of Stimlje was shot at, and a policeman was killed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name. The witness is again speaking extremely fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are speaking very fast, but are you reading from something, Mrs. Marinkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're reading from a note made when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 15th of January, 1999. On the day when I first entered Racak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Well, I had asked you for the bases for your conclusion that the men were members of the KLA. So far you have been telling me that you had information that the KLA were active in the area a few days prior to the Racak incident. Any more specific bases for concluding that they were members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concrete evidence on site. When I carried out the on-site investigation, I found weapons, I found their headquarters where there were uniforms, and I found lists, duty rosters of different shifts of their members who were on duty, and in the house where their headquarters where was the kitchen where they got their food. Also, there was a warehouse where there was a large quantity of food. Then trenches that criss-crossed the area, and there was a countless number of casings of ammunition from automatic weapons, and also a bunker where they forgot a machine-gun nest and they were operating from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean they forgot the tripod?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Also, I can tell you that the 40 bodies we found in the mosque were dressed in civilian clothes. However, some men wore grey woolen military trousers. Most of them had military boots. They had identical leather belts, and we found that some of them had other layers of clothing, two or three underneath the clothes they were wearing. Everything I found there on site and after the post-mortem was carried out and after we collected all information or, rather, after authorised personnel collected all information, and when this written -- this information was submitted in written form, all of this indicated that it was terrorists who were in the village of Racak, not civilians. Secondly, three days before, I tried and when I succeeded on the fourth day to enter Racak, I was shot at all the time, and the members of my team were shot at too. Fire was directed at us from all sides, even on the 18th. As the on-site investigation was coming to an end, I was shot at, the members of the team were shot at, the members of the OSCE were shot at, and we were forced to seek shelter and run. We were followed by gunfire as we were leaving Racak. Even the vehicle where I was was hit, and other members of the investigation team were there too. Fortunately, it was an armoured vehicle, so I managed to survive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have one more question. Two, actually. You said you found a duty roster. Do the names in that match with the list, with the names you have for post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, believe me, I just can't remember now. Yesterday, when we looked at the footage, I heard them read out the names of the people who were on the list, but I really can't say now. I can't remember. It was a long time ago. But the lists were confiscated and as evidence they are in the set of files linked to Racak. So you can compare them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And my last question: So where do you think we could find that duty roster that you found at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's like this: After we completed the investigation, I handed over the complete set of evidence and files to the authorised public prosecutor in Pristina. So the case went to him and the case should be located in the district court in Pristina, which at the moment we don't have access to. Perhaps you yourselves could come by that -- those files. That's as far as I know, because when I completed my investigation and when I received the findings, analyses and conclusions of the post-mortems, I handed over all the files and records there, and I have an Official Note saying I did that. On the 1st of March, 1999, it says, I gave to the official public prosecutor of the district court in Pristina, I gave all this material, and the number is 3/14/99 of that file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. And as for the boy whom Mr. Milosevic referred to whose name I remember as Beqiri Halim, do you have any idea yourself how the boy was killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, do you remember how many names you saw on the duty roster and what period was covered in relation to their duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I can remember now - because I did see the lists and there was the typewriter they type wrote the lists on - according to the duty roster there were shifts, one shift in the morning from morning until 3.00 p.m., then from 3.00 to 5.00 p.m. They worked in three shifts and what I remember is that on one of the lists it said that for that particular day two men who were supposed to be on duty were sick and were relieved of duty, and they had their small clinic in Racak's infirmary where they would go if they were sick and then they would be relieved of duty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, perhaps I could help with that question. Yesterday, I heard a voice when we saw the footage that was played when they were looking at the material at the headquarters, I heard a voice mention at the base, I heard a date the 24th of December, I think, and another day in December. So that was several weeks prior to the event, the dates that you could hear on the tape that was played yesterday. There was a voice mentioning two dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also heard the voice of the interpreter together with my voice when we played that footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, you said that as of the 1st of March, you passed the papers in the case or your report on the case to the prosecutor. What is the nature of the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the case is under a Kri number, that was 14/99, which is a book of records where we keep all the reports on the investigation, on-site investigation conducted by the investigating authorised judge. So it is linked to the scene of crime investigations, and all the evidence that is amassed and collected is placed in one file and handed over to the prosecutor. That means that everything I did as the investigating judge -- I completed my work on the investigation. Everything I have collected, including my own -- what I saw on the spot, all the research I did, my orders for the post-mortems to be carried out, my order for identification to be carried out, that complete set of material I handed over to the authorised prosecutor to assess and see whether there was good cause to take the matter further or to seek additional explanations, reports, and so on. So it is up to him to ask the SUP to carry on the investigation on the spot if he feels he needs to have more material and evidence, or he can ask me to carry on additional investigation if he deems necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, a practical question for you now. During the investigation and the expertise and in keeping with the provisions of crime investigation for individual cases, did you check out and investigate whether the individuals who were the subject of forensic investigations used firearms, for example?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the order I issued giving instructions and guidelines to the crime investigation service of the SUP in Pristina, what steps they should take, one of my orders includes this, and I think you have my order in the file.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Just give me a brief answer now, please.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the bodies that were found in the mosque, paraffin gloves were taken in order to establish the gunpowder traces on their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And how many of the people that were examined on the basis of that paraffin-glove test was it established had actually fired from a firearm?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was established on 37 of the bodies. There were gunpowder traces which showed that they had come into contact with firearms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Marinkovic, the police organs, prior to the event of the 15th of January, did they have data and information about Racak and the surrounding villages, Malopoljce, Petrovo Selo, Rance, the surrounding villages and hamlets, that general area, that they represent a firm stronghold of the terrorists? Did they have information of that kind?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the basis of what can you say that? What grounds do you have for claiming that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be allowed to answer? Can I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have been through that already, Mr. Milosevic. You're going over the same ground.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, let's take a look at a few tabs, Mrs. Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, gentlemen, I'd like to draw your attention that you have all this material. And the English text is far more legible than my Serbian version because I have photocopies which are fairly poor photocopies, illegible, but nonetheless, you can read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 46, we have a piece of information which is set out on four pages, and that was compiled by authorised persons. They are listed at the end. And this is what that report says. It is dated the 20th of January, 1999, and at the beginning of the report notice taken of the facts that in June 1998, in the village of Racak, in the mosque, a meeting of members of the so-called KLA was held, and then it says who led the meeting. That's not important for us at the moment. And then it talks about the establishment of subheadquarters for Racak, for the village of Petrovo, Ljuzak Mahala, and Malopoljce. And then it goes on to explain where the subheadquarters for the village of Racak is located, substaffs, where they were put up, located. It goes on to explain that for a brief period of time Afet Bilali was appointed or was the acting commander of the staff or substaff. And it also says who dealt with the rear and logistics; Lutfi Bilali, his brother Qerim, Ameti, and so on -- well, my question is this: In view of the fact that on the one but last page, under number 3, or page number 3, there is a long list of all the people who were there. Can we see from this that a number of people were from the village of Racak? Some of them were from Racak, others were from Malopoljce, for example, and the Kacanik area, Lipjan area, Suva Reka, and so on. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be of assistance here with respect to this report? On page 2, for example, it says that they collected money.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, all right, but I'm not interested in that in particular. But since you mentioned paragraph 2, it says: "On the basis of operative knowledge, we have information that in the village of Racak there were over 100 members of the KLA." That's what it says here. So was that the information that you received? It says, "Based on operative information, we have details..." et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the penultimate paragraph talks about how they armed themselves and said they had hand grenades, snipers, automatic rifles, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The accused just said that this is the information received. Is it right you received? Could you tell me, first of all, what this document is about. Is this the information you received at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's like this: This report was compiled by the authorised persons of the SUP in Urosevac. It is under number 6/99, and the date is the 20th of January, 1999. This information or report is contained in the bulletin of the Urosevac SUP. It is a bulletin that they put out on a daily basis, including all information of this kind, and they send on to the prosecutor's office and the court. So every day we would receive information, a bulletin, a report of what they were doing in the field, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this was written or filed after the Racak incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But it also includes what happened the previous day, and this was done as of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The events from June on, actually, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, this was something that was written after the Racak massacre, referring to events beforehand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The events were ones that happened before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And these events must have been recorded in other documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the bulletins, the official bulletins of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we don't have the bulletins.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It all remained over there. It's all over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to add something, give an additional explanation? Linked to all this, the events that took place before and after Racak, official reports were filed by the officials, authorised persons, and those criminal reports were sent on to the public prosecutor, for kidnappings, killings, abductions, and so on. Official criminal reports were filed, and the SUP went out onto the scene of the crime and wrote minutes of what was found. Now, I was prevented, for security reasons, from going to the scene, so I authorised official persons to conduct an on-site investigation instead of me, and I am authorised by the law to do so. So in certain criminal reports that were sent on to the public prosecutor, for instance, in the criminal report it states that the investigating judge was informed that an on-scene investigation that was carried out, that such-and-such was established, and then all those files were sent to the prosecutor, and there are a large number of criminal reports for that period of time for all crimes committed by the terrorists during that period of time where legal proceedings were initiated as a result.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Marinkovic. Now, if we see here on page 3, for example, paragraph 2, the month of December 1998 and January 1999 says: "Members of the so-called KLA in the village of Racak dug trenches and bunkers above the village of Racak in the direction of the village of Petrovo, Rance and towards the main Stimlje-Crnoljevo road," et cetera, et cetera. When you came on the scene, you saw the bunkers, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You saw the trenches that were dug, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So if we were to compare what it says here in this report, and every report refers to the time before the -- the incident that happened before the report was compiled, is that right?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So everything that happened you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I walked through the trenches. I saw them and walked through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You talked about -- mention is made of the substaff. You were in the staff, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So are you going to accept this as an exhibit? Is this going to be exhibited, Mr. Robinson? This is an official report by the official body.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I make one observation on the admissibility of this as a document. It's obviously not the witness's document, not her report. The person preparing the report has relied on sources of information which are themselves, it would appear, sometimes perhaps secondhand and we don't have those original sources of information so it's a very difficult document for us to deal with. The question for the Chamber whether it's sufficiently satisfied that it can be of some evidential value, but this remove of hearsay and information might take it outside that category. It's up to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Well, it's an official document that passed through her hands at the time, so therefore it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Albeit after the event, but we'll admit it. It goes to weight. And there's an earlier document that the witness used, her own list of the -- of the bodies that she found, which should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not in the binder. Could you get that from the witness, Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the accused wishes to exhibit it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is just a document showing that the indictment does not operate with accurate facts 16 years after the event -- six years after the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A copy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document will be numbered Exhibit D291.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But make a copy and return it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I don't think we dealt with tabs 45, yesterday, did we, to formally make them exhibits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I remind you that you must ensure that the exhibits that you wish to have tendered, you must bring them to our attention. 45 was the -- what was 45?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The video clips.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 45 are exclusively CDs, video footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit those.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look now at tab 47. It contains a statement of an ethnic Albanian by the name of Shemsi Emini, signed by him. The statement was given on the 11th of February, 1999. All his personal details are on record here. He's of Yugoslav identification, personal identification number, the number of his ID. I won't dwell on that. He says that in June 1998, a meeting was held in Racak, attended by the villagers, and the meeting was chaired --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, just lay the foundation. You have been doing this long enough now to know. Don't just move to the document. Lay the foundation for her to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I laid the foundation for all these statements because I asked her already to name the grounds for stating that Racak, Malopoljce, Rance and this narrower area of Racak was a major stronghold of the KLA, and the witness answered based on reports collected, information and evidence. I'm asking her now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Among the other information that was available to you, did you have this statement given by Shemsi Emini? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does this statement coincide in terms of information with the previous report we saw in tab 46?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the passage -- the paragraph not far from the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what is more important to the Judges is not the content of the document at this moment. How was this statement taken? Was this document part of the official record, and how was this document taken? Those are more important issues. That's what the Presiding Judge emphasised: Just lay the foundation of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, is this statement part of the official record that includes everything, the entire evidence you collected during your investigation in Racak?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a statement taken by authorised personnel, authorised officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's my separate question. Who took the statement? Were they authorised officers?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was the statement taken in the proper form in which authorised officers are required to take statements from citizens?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I will read out to you the end of this large passage --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just to make an observation without repeating myself if similar statements are going to be dealt with. I've made my position, I think, clear in earlier discussion about statements of this kind. I've made observations about whether statements of this kind should be adduced if at all through the process of 92 bis or 89(F), and I have sought to draw similarities between the material contained in this kind of document and the material that was excluded when it was sought to summarise evidence of this kind or broadly similar kind through the evidence of Barney Kelly. So my objections to this document are simply a repetition of arguments I've made before, but I announce them. And if the document is admitted in, I shan't stand up to repeat my objection in respect to any similar ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We understand that. We know this is an official document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the exhibit number the Prosecution just tendered? I'll find out. Give me a -- Exhibit 837 and 838. Those are witness statements. Some of them are under seal, but the Prosecution didn't tender it under 89(F) or 92 bis, Mr. Nice. Mr. Nice, I don't see a point you are emphasising the regime of 89(F) or 92 bis at this stage. The Prosecution itself is not tendering the statements under those regimes now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Not now it isn't, no. In fact, the reference to 89(F) and 92 bis I think was raised by, initially in this part of our discussion on procedures, by Your Honour in relation to I think it was statements that were tendered or proposed to be tendered by either Andric or -- I think it was by Andric, and the contemplation then was that this was, as it were, an exhaustive process for the tendering of documents that were in this general form and prepared for court purposes, but I think the debate has moved on since then and indeed the Chamber has admitted two documents produced by the Prosecution, or one document in statement form, maybe the one Your Honour's referring to, since that debate started. But, Your Honour, the position remains that the Prosecution does not accept that all statements -- we understand the rule about hearsay, but statements of this kind which come from witnesses we aren't able to cross-examine, if the witnesses are available and if there's no other foundation laid for why they should be produced in this way, we would respectfully argue should not be admitted in this format but I'm not going to repeat the arguments that we've set out here and indeed elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson. Mr. Robinson. The witness we have here is an investigating judge, the investigating judge who performed the investigation in Racak. This document is part of the official record reflecting the work of the investigating judge, a part of the official record of the investigation she performed, and such official notes and reports and statements are numerous. The information in them matches mutually and the investigating judge is sitting right across from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. I think you have put it very well. Continue, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So, at the end of this only long passage, it says: "... I saw the following people wearing uniforms with KLA insignia and armed with automatic rifles: Nuhi Jakupi, who was among the first to join the KLA; Rifat Imeri; Idriz Mehmeti; Mehmet Agusi..." and so on and so forth. He keeps enumerating people that he had seen. And then he says, "The commander of the Racak substaff was Afet Bilali, also known as Copa ..." He also says that Sadik Mujota was also in Racak. This Sadik Mujota which he says was accompanied with his sons, was Sadik Mujota also one of the prominent members of this terrorist organisation, according to your information?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Many reports collected by authorised officers confirmed this, corroborate this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the tab 47 exhibited, please, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you now look at tab 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, this statement under tab 48, is it part of the official documentation you reviewed? It's a statement given by Serif Sadiki.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was it possible to establish -- is it possible to establish that this statement was given on the 12th of January, three days before the Racak incident?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This statement, was it also taken by authorised office --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I don't follow this. I'm lost. How and why was the investigation on already on 12th of January? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. On what case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned to you earlier in my testimony that for a while, starting with September, October 1998, in Racak, in the area surrounding Racak, there were abductions, kidnappings, killings, victimising Serbs, Albanians, the Roma. There were attacks on police patrols causing deaths of policemen. Houses of villagers who refused to join the KLA were torched. And in connection with all those terrorists activities, the police continuously collected operative information on the ground. This information indicated that Racak was a major stronghold of the terrorist gang called the KLA. I have a large file of material that I was not able to bring here, but the police in Urosevac has many, many case files dealing with all these cases, because every single case was accompanied by a criminal report submitted to the district public prosecutor. And I can add, as you will see from the Official Notes that follow, the names mentioned in those statements taken from citizens in the pre-criminal proceedings match with the names of killed persons on the list that I have, which indicates, seems to indicate that they were members of the terrorist gangs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have them here with me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I'm bearing in mind that all these documents that I am quoting can be viewed easily later once they are exhibited, and we can compare the names. Some were killed in battle, some fled. Some were perhaps involved in other assignments at the time of the incident. But all these statements indicate the presence of the terrorist gang in Racak and the surrounding villages. Since you have information about all that was going on in 1998, including the large number of terrorist attacks, let me remind you that many more Albanians than Serbs were killed as a result of terrorist acts in 1998. And you heard the testimony of Mr. Hartwig and saw his reports --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this statement related to Racak that was given on the 12th of January, 1999, he mentions that: "In Racak I saw Smail Musliu and Nebi Smail and Shyqeri Smaili wearing KLA uniforms before the house of Bilali Lutfi, where humanitarian aid was collected." And he said, "I heard recently that two members of the KLA had been wounded on the hill above the old peoples home in Racak village. One of them from the Kacanik area are being treated at the -- is being treated at the outpatients clinic." And then he says, "I'm not certain, but I think there are between 50 and 100 members of the KLA in Racak village." Ms. Marinkovic, does this piece of information fit with the other information collected by authorised officers? This is the statement given by Sadiki Serif.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. Especially it fits with the reports drafted by the police in Urosevac dated the 20th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it precisely based on such information collected on the ground that official persons, in this case policemen of Urosevac, make their reports?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, may this tab as well, 48, be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 49, there is an Official Note which was compiled on the 28th of January, 1999. Was that Official Note part of the records that you worked on in connection with the investigation of Racak?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this the customary way of writing official notes? It says Official Note, here, number 36/1999, Urosevac, "Compiled on the 28th of January, 1999, with regard to information about the death of Racak villagers who were members of the so-called KLA."

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then here it says further on: "Through friendly information channels we learned that the following three members of the so-called KLA were killed in the clash with Siptar terrorists in Racak village, Stimlje municipality in mid-January this year: Sharamet Syla, Kadri Syla, and Shyqeri Syla."

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "The Official Note is hereby forwarded for further processing." What does this -- what does this mean "through operative channels," "information channels," "friendly information channels"? What does that mean in an Official Note of the Secretariat of the Interior and when such two officials sign a note?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Operative channels" means that authorised personnel spoke to a person whose identity they are protecting because he is an informant of theirs and therefore, due to security reasons, his name cannot be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you look at the names mentioned here, the names of the killed persons referred to in this note? Are they on the list or not?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These three persons mentioned in this Official Note, when compared to the list of identified corpses that appeared in Racak, there is Syla Shyqeri and Syla Sharamet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The third person does not appear there?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is sufficient explanation.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my list, if you want to have a look at it, it is corpse number 18, Syla Sharamet, and corpse number 20, Syla Shyqeri.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to what it says in this Official Note, two out of the three mentioned persons coincide with that -- with persons on that list of 40.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: One person's name cannot be found on that list.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please exhibit tab 49.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before that is done, I think this may be the first time, or my recollection of the first time that the Chamber has been confronted with information that is expressly based on intelligence where the source of the intelligence can't be given. That's my understanding of what the witness is saying. And that may or may not be a new factor that the Chamber would want to consider before admitting the document. Of course, the only pursuit that the Prosecution could make would be of the preparer of the document, if at all, it appearing that providing the person who prepares the document sticks with the line advanced by the witness, we won't be able to get back to the source of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We've dealt with that before, and what we have said is that it's a matter that you can take up in cross-examination and eventually it will be for the Chamber to determine what weight to attach to the evidence, but we don't think it invalidates the admissibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I may be wrong in my recollection, but the characteristic of this that may be different is that this is actually relying on information that is expressly confidential or secret. It would be like, I suppose, a Prosecution witness coming along and saying he or she had been provided by the intelligence services of country X or Y with information to the following effect. I don't believe that's happened before in this trial. I mean, it's a long time and sometimes one forgets things, but I don't believe we've ever reached that position before. And many -- in many jurisdictions it would be regarded as unusual. But I don't want it take any more time. That's my additional point on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The unusual nature of it would be because in a domestic jurisdiction the prosecutor might oppose its admission and there might be national security grounds for doing so, but here we have a situation where a party's tendering it and you don't have a basis for opposing it on that sort of ground. Now, this document's offered as a piece of material which was in the hand of the witness in the course of her investigation, and for that reason alone it must be admissible. The question will have to be addressed later, whether it could be viewed as evidence supportive of the truth of its contents. That's quite a separate issue, I think, on which you will no doubt address us later, but it seems to me you couldn't resist its exhibition on the basis that its material in her hands at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If the -- if evidence of the witness's opinion is in itself of value to the Chamber, as opposed to the accuracy of opinion, that is the evidence -- if evidence of what her opinion was is of value to the Chamber, then I can see that supporting material can have independent admissibility criteria on that ground alone, but once we move beyond the fact of what her opinion was to its accuracy, then one could object to the admissibility of supporting material that is simply not accessible to us in any way for examination and cross-examination. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I've been looking, Mr. Nice, at some of the situations presented by the Prosecution in the course of its case, and we even get, on occasions, to the point of what was the rumour or what was the word on the street, more or less, and that's come in as evidence, which we will have to at some stage adjudicate upon. We will have to decide whether it has got any weight at all. Probably in that case it hasn't got any, but it's there and it was led in answer to specific -- indeed, on one occasion I saw, it was followed up. So this is no different in character, I would suggest, from some of the material that was given orally in the course of the Prosecution evidence. Just because it comes in writing it doesn't seem to me that it therefore has a different status.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I accept entirely there's been a wide range of evidence given. I repeat my observation that I think this is the first time - I may be wrong - the first time that we've had material that is expressly protected on grounds of this kind of secrecy, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you for the submissions, Mr. Nice. Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on again now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, in your investigation, did you have in your hands this statement which is provided in tab 50, Shaban Rama's statement on the 16th of January, 1999? All his details were taken. Did you have this statement in your hands?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it part of the records that you compiled, the evidence that you compiled in relation to Racak?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Shaban Rama says that in KLA uniforms recently and with PU insignia. What is this PU insignia? Did you manage to establish that during your investigation?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is insignia worn by what they call their special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So this is a terrorist organisation, the KLA, which has some kind of a special group, too, bearing PU insignia.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what this abbreviation is in Albanian, this PU?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: P, I assume, is police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But what about the U?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Milosevic. Is Jasovic, Sparavalo, or Vujnovic, those persons who seem to have taken this document, this statement, are they from part of your team at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are authorised officers of the Urosevac SUP but at the time when I was carrying out the on-site investigation they were not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where did they take this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, usually either on the ground or in the office. A citizen would come and report something, and if the citizen wants to be interviewed by the official, then the statement is taken in the official's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This says that this statement was taken on 16th of January, when you were shot at at the Racak village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So this is done apart from your on-site investigation. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, I assume that that's it, because as for my work in relation to Racak, some witnesses, inhabitants of Racak stated that they had left the village of Racak before the action had started. So the village was empty. Villagers who were not members of the KLA were simply not there, people who did not want to take part in any kind of action. So they moved either to Stimlje or to Urosevac to stay with relatives, with their families. I assume that this is one such witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I noticed most of the questions put to these witnesses are who were those who were -- who are the KLA members. So the main purpose of this investigation is to identify the members of the KLA. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. To identify them and to establish the fact that in Racak there was a major terrorist stronghold.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just bear this explanation in mind: In all those years, starting from 1992, as you can see from the records, the police tried to establish who members of the KLA were, and some were arrested on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can put the question to the witness instead of commenting yourself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, just wait a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the first 20-minute break. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Marinkovic, we're talking about this critical period of time, 1998, 1997, further back, but for the most part in 1998. Were most of the KLA killings made from ambush?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were some of the killings in the area that you're talking about, Racak, Malopoljce, Rance, committed in that way before the incident in Racak that we're talking about? And I'm referring to the area of the SUP of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So on the basis of instructions issued to the police by the investigating trial judge, was the task of the police to uncover who members of the KLA were and it was their activities that led to such a large number of victims?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm looking at tab 50, the statement of Shaban Rama. Was that part of that endeavour to uncover members of the KLA who were committing Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. these crimes?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Mr. Robinson, could you admit into evidence the statement contained in tab 50.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to add something. There are two names that are mentioned in this statement, that these persons were killed on the 15th of January, 1998, by terrorists of the KLA. I have them on the list of the 40 persons, and the names are Bilali Lutfi and Emini Ajet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the names because it was very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of January, during armed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic and the witness, Judge Marinkovic, you're overlapping. The interpreters are asking you once again to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I asked to have this statement admitted into evidence. It is part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of the records on which Judge Marinkovic worked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's my mistake probably, but I managed to find on the document one of the names that she's referring to as being a member of the KLA. That's towards the bottom in the block of text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Bilali Lutfi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's that one, but the other one, it must be my mistake, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm trying too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I obviously need to know this material in some degree of detail if I'm to prepare sensibly to cross-examine, and obviously if I'm able to establish that these people were members of the KLA I shall make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The other one is on the schedule and is one of those who the witness said was common to both her inquiry and --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes, it's just I haven't found the name. The other one is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the other name is Hacif Hisenaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I've got it, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what I heard was Ajet Emini, so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So did I, so I was confused.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter said at that point that it was extremely fast and it was very hard to keep up, and the other members of the team managed to find it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that it's on now. I see the light on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Dzeljadin Muhadini, an Albanian; and if so, how do you know the name?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the name because he also made a statement in pre-trial proceedings to authorised personnel on the 17th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That the statement that you had in your own proceedings and which is contained in tab 51? Muhadini Dzeljadin, on the 17th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this statement, he claims that he is a permanent resident of the hamlet of Cesta in the village of Racak, Stimlje municipality, and he says: "Since two months ago, my family and I have been temporarily residing at the house of Muhamet Rexhaj, a friend of mine, in Stimlje." He left Racak, therefore, two months prior to what happened. The villagers of Racak, they left Racak. Is that what you established? And in Racak there weren't any residents, any villagers at the time of the event?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I mentioned yesterday, when I entered the village of Racak, there was not a single civilian there that I found. It was abandoned and empty, the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this statement, he mentions the following members of the KLA who were killed in Racak on the 15th of January: Sadik Mujota, with his daughter, whose name he does not know; Shaqa Shaqiri, from the village of Racak. He's referring to the ones he saw in camouflage uniform with KLA insignia; Enver Rashiti from the village of Racak, a member of the KLA in the village of Laniste. Kadri Ismajli from the village of Racak. Lutfi Bilali from the village of Racak, and Nijazi Zymberi from the village of Racak. And then he mentions an individual whose first and last name he does not know. He knows that he is from the area of Kacanik and a member of the KLA. He was killed 200 metres away from the KLA substaff in the village of Racak. And then the commander of the substaff for the village of Racak, Afet Bilali, was seriously wounded and taken to a place unknown to him for further medical treatment. Is that the information that you had in mind during the course of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He says: "While I lived in the village of Racak, security at the village of Cesta--" "While I was living in the village of Racak," and he says he lived in the hamlet of Cesta, "dressed in uniforms with KLA insignia," the following were involved and armed with infantry weapons, Sadik Mujota, Mehmet Mustafa, Shaqa Shaqiri, and the brothers Idriz and Bajram Mehmeti and son of Mehmet Agushi. He also mentioned a piece of information that we saw in former statements. He says: "A month ago, two KLA members were wounded," and he gives their names, and the same name of the doctor who treated them. Now, did you compare these statements and all the facts contained in them and deal with all that during your investigation into Racak?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he mentioned two individuals here as having been killed in the village of Racak as members of the KLA, and they are Bilali Lutfi and Zymberi Nijazi.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do they coincide with the names on your lists?

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I mean the list of persons who were -- or corpses taken from the mosque to be forensically examined.

utterances.speaker: DANICA MARINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I think that Zymberi Nijazi was just mentioned here in the interpretation. I said Bilali Lutfi as well. That's the second man.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm sure that will be put right in the record. What you have in front of you is the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
